open_points.subject: record_change
open_points.text: record_change: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] A StoredValue whose value_id already exists is not written again, since equal values share one identity. A StoredValue carries no bytes: the bytes of every StoredValue a change names MUST already be published under its value_digest by the caller with put_value_bytes before the change, as spooled files must already be published in the run's spool by spool_file before the change that writes their SpooledFile records; record_change publishes, rewrites and re-checks no value bytes and no spooled file, and writes only records.
open_points.other_text: record_change: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] Durability order: every file a change names is published, fsynced and its directory fsynced before the change is committed, and the SQLite database runs with synchronous FULL, so after a power loss a committed record never names a missing or partial file; a file published by a change that then failed stays unnamed: a value file until the next start removes it, a spooled file until it is replaced at its position or its run's spool is removed (A18 rule 4).
open_points.question: Must value and spooled files be published by record_change as part of the change, or must they be published by callers before record_change so that a failed change merely leaves previously published files unnamed?

open_points.rule: Владелец такой ноты — caller/callsite, не callee.
open_points.question: Move the requirements that callers invoke put_value_bytes and spool_file before record_change to the notes of the respective callers/callsites, leaving the record_change note to state only its own preconditions and behavior.
